content.title: Everything to Know About Tonight's Women's March Madness Bracket Reveal
content.text: Key PointsSelection Sunday is March 15, 2026, with the women's show airing on ESPN.UConn, UCLA, Texas, and South Carolina are projected No. 1 seeds; UConn enters undefeated.ESPN airs the entire tournament; Final Four and championship are on ABC for wider access. 2026 Women’s March Madness has everything. We’re talking an undefeated team chasing history, a stunning conference championship upset and bubble drama, too. LSU’s Kim Mulkey will most certainly dress to impress—and coach to win—while Iowa State’s Audi Crooks will be doing what she does best: cooking in the paint and playing with the kind of heart that brings tears to your eyes. Whether you’re a longtime women’s hoops fan who’s had a year-round countdown going, or you’re just discovering that this side of March Madness hits just as hard (spoiler: it does), here’s everything you need to know about Women’s Selection Sunday 2026. 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 When Is Selection Sunday 2026? Selection Sunday is this Sunday, March 15, 2026. What Time Does Selection Sunday Start? The women’s bracket reveal begins at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN. You can also stream it on the ESPN app or ESPN+ with a cable login. Additional streaming options include DirecTV, YouTubeTV, Hulu + Live TV and FuboTV. How Does Selection Sunday Work? If you read our men’s Selection Sunday guide, you already know the basics. Here’s the quick version. Just like the men’s tournament, the women’s field features 68 teams. Thirty-one spots go to conference tournament champions (automatic bids) and the remaining 37 are at-large bids chosen by the NCAA Selection Committee. Here’s what makes the women’s tournament unique: the top 16 seeds host the first and second round games on their home courts. That means powerhouses like UConn and South Carolina get to play in front of their own fans in the opening rounds—and if you’ve ever seen a sold-out arena full of women’s basketball fans, you know the energy is unmatched. The committee reveals the full bracket during the show: all 68 teams, their seedings—ranked 1 through 16 in four regions—and their first-round matchups. And just like the men’s side, the real drama comes from the bubble teams—the ones sweating it out, waiting to hear their name called. UConn’s Sarah Strong is the frontrunner for National Player of the Year as the Huskies enter March Madness with an undefeated record.Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images And if you want to get your women’s hoops fix before the first round kicks off this week, there’s no shortage of storylines heading into Selection Sunday. UConn enters the tournament a perfect 34-0, riding a 50-game winning streak and chasing a record 13th national title—and they’re doing it without Paige Bueckers, who left for the WNBA after last year’s championship run. Sophomore Sarah Strong has stepped into the spotlight as the frontrunner for National Player of the Year, and senior guard Azzi Fudd—last year’s Final Four MVP and projected No. 1 pick in the 2026 WNBA draft—is having the best season of her career right alongside her. If UConn runs the table, they’d be just the seventh team in history to finish as undefeated champions. Meanwhile, Texas stunned three-time defending SEC tournament champion South Carolina 78-61 last weekend behind tournament MVP Madison Booker, who dropped 18 points as the Longhorns opened the game on a jaw-dropping 14-0 run. (I’d highly suggest watching the highlights!) And on the bubble, keep an eye on Richmond—they’re sitting right on the “last team in” line after losing to George Mason in the A-10 semifinals, and their fate could be sealed by tonight’s Ivy League championship game between Princeton and Harvard. If Princeton loses, two Ivy teams could make the field, and that could bump the Spiders right out. Meanwhile, Stanford—once projected as a No. 7 seed—won’t be dancing at all this year after losing eight of ten games down the stretch and getting bounced early from the ACC tournament. It’s the second straight year that Stanford has missed the Big Dance since Tara VanDerveer’s retirement. Texas’ Madison Booker and South Carolina’s Agot Makeer battled twice this season—and both teams are projected No. 1 seeds heading into tomorrow’s bracket reveal.Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images Who Are the Projected No. 1 Seeds? UConn UCLA Texas South Carolina What Is the Full 2026 Women’s NCAA Tournament Schedule? Selection Sunday: March 15, 8 p.m. ET on ESPN First Four: March 18–19 First Round: March 20–21 Second Round: March 22–23 Sweet 16: March 27–28 (Fort Worth, TX & Sacramento, CA) Elite Eight: March 29–30 (Fort Worth, TX & Sacramento, CA) Final Four: April 3 (Phoenix, AZ — Mortgage Matchup Center) National Championship: April 5, 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC (Phoenix, AZ — Mortgage Matchup Center) How to Watch March Madness Games After Selection Sunday The entire women’s tournament airs across ESPN’s family of networks—ESPN, ESPN2 and ESPNU—with games also streaming on the ESPN app and ESPN+. The Final Four and national championship move to network TV on ABC, so no cable subscription is needed for the biggest games of the tournament. Did you know it was only five years ago—in 2021—that ABC broadcast a women’s tournament game? In fact, I’m old enough to remember when women’s tournament games were buried on obscure channels at random tip-off times, so watching these programs and athletes finally get the attention and airtime they deserve is really special. How Can I Fill Out or Print a Bracket? ESPN’s free Women’s Tournament Challenge lets you fill out your bracket online and compete with friends—and honestly, it’s one of the most fun parts of March Madness. You can also print a blank bracket directly from NCAA.com once the selections are revealed. Stay tuned to Parade.com for daily tournament updates! Next, When Is Selection Sunday 2026?
